subject.summary: Occupational definition | O*NET-SOC43-5011.01 researches freight rates, routes and transport modes, understands regulations governing international cargo movement, and arranges additional services such as storage and inland transport. The 31 tasks include rate negotiation; special transport for sensitive cargo such as livestock, food and medical supplies; duties, taxes and customs clearance; informing customers of options and deadlines; bills of lading, packing lists, dock receipts and certificates of origin; invoices and quotations; choosing routes by cargo, timing and safety; weight/volume/cost calculations; delivery and storage; multimodal transport and environmental optimization; paying or arranging freight and insurance charges; in-transit and receipt/dispatch records; booking, insurance and consolidation; port information; packaging, labeling and document checks; regulatory and political developments; packaging advice; referrals to specialists such as trade finance experts; cooperation with customs brokers; examining carriers' environmental records and route/packaging sustainability; and assisting insurance claims. Official tasks include payments, customs clearance and claims assistance and cannot be excluded categorically. Verify jurisdiction, job procedures and authority separately; task lists do not directly grant authorization.
